prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: production pixel-art animation sprite master for a tiny native 32x32 boss in a side-view garden roguelite. Input image: identity and exact pixel-style reference, containing eight poses of this boss. Expand the SAME creature into a sheet with EXACTLY FOUR COLUMNS and EIGHT ROWS, 32 fully drawn DIFFERENT animation poses. Transparent background. Equally sized cells; no labels, text, grid lines, frame numbers or borders. Every sprite faces right. Keep the same creature proportions, body mass, dark silhouette, outline colors and muted pixel clusters as the reference. Draw authentic coarse native low-resolution pixel art, not illustration: hard square pixel blocks, no smooth edges, no antialiasing, no gradient, no glow, no shadow. Design within a notional 32x32 grid per frame; legs and actions stay within the cell. All cells have the same camera and scale and fixed central foot anchor at the bottom, with generous transparent gutters. Change anatomical poses and silhouettes instead of copying a sprite and translating or rotating it. Limited colors: darkest teal #10171c, #1d2b34, #2b4645, moss #3d5146 #536448, bark #605047 #82725b, pale cream #b5b190 #d7d4b1, muted plum #493650 #847088, icy grey #547580 #98b0b0. Amber accents ONLY in row 3 windup. Cyan accents ONLY in row 6 exposed vulnerability. Each row is its own ordered four-pose animation read left to right. Use all 32 cells. No empty cells. Do not draw detached projectiles outside the sprite.

Frostjaw identity: squat dark teal spiky beetle or crab body with icy pale heavy mandibles, short articulated legs, jagged frost crown. Preserve the reference. Row 1 idle: mandibles slightly ajar, left palp twitches, jaw clacks shut, icy dorsal spines shiver. Row 2 movement: four articulated crab-beetle scuttling steps, opposing legs reach and push, jaw countersways. Row 3 windup: legs plant wide, icy mandibles open wider, body crouches and amber throat appears, jaws tense at widest opening. Row 4 attack: pincers extend forward, upper mandible snaps down, lower mandible slams up, both clack closed with two tiny pale shard pixels near the jaw. Row 5 recovery: body hunches, legs spread braking, jaw hangs open tired, returns to guard. Row 6 vulnerable: chest plates spread revealing cyan inner throat, jaw tilts up, soft core swells, body shivers leaving core exposed. Row 7 hurt: head recoil and one mandible kicked up, opposite leg buckles, body curls and ice crown cracks, legs catch. Row 8 death: legs collapse out, head rests on soil, shell fractures into two attached pieces, low icy broken husk with both mandibles on soil. Every frame anatomically distinct.
